report.title: Activity: Review and complete a sample size calculation report

segments.text: The trial asks whether neravixa increases four-week pain relief compared with duloxetine. Adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, bilateral lower-extremity pain due to diabetic peripheral neuropathy for at least one year, and BMI at least 18 and below 40 kg/m² will be individually randomized 1:1. Each participant contributes one yes-or-no pain-relief outcome, assessed in the same way in both groups.
segments.explanation: The population, comparison, allocation and primary outcome with its assessment time are specified. Individual randomization and one outcome per participant support the proposed independent-group comparison.
segments.heading: Question and design

segments.text: The pilot observed relief in 7 of 10 patients receiving neravixa and 3 of 10 receiving duloxetine. Because these small groups leave substantial uncertainty, the target difference is set at 30 percentage points. Patient and clinical advisers consider 20 points the minimum worthwhile increase to justify the additional monitoring visits and risk of dizziness. Differences are expressed as neravixa minus duloxetine.
segments.explanation: The pilot observation, target difference and clinical threshold have distinct, justified roles. Their numerical values can coincide in other studies.
segments.section: Observed difference, target difference and clinical threshold
segments.heading: Assumptions and evidence

segments.text: The calculation therefore assumes 70% relief with neravixa and 30% with duloxetine. At a two-sided Type I error probability of 5% and 90% power, 56 analyzable patients are required per group.
segments.explanation: The stated percentages differ by 40 points, while the selected target is 30 points. The 56-per-group result uses 60% versus 30%. A consistent revision is: “The calculation assumes 60% relief with neravixa and 30% with duloxetine. At a two-sided Type I error probability of 5% and 90% power, 56 analyzable patients are required per group.”
segments.heading: Calculation

segments.text: A power of 90% means that the planned test would detect a difference in about 90 of 100 repeated trials if the population relief percentages were 60% and 30% and the other assumptions held.
segments.explanation: This interpretation connects power to repeated trials under the specified population assumptions. It also makes the inconsistency in the preceding calculation inputs visible.

segments.text: The primary outcome will be compared using a standard statistical test. The sample size was calculated in R.
segments.explanation: The procedure and software record are incomplete. The report should specify a two-sided pooled score test for independent proportions without continuity correction, the normal planning approximation in stats::power.prop.test(), alternative = “two.sided”, strict = TRUE, and the R and stats versions. The recorded command should reproduce the stated inputs and result.

segments.text: The required analyzable sample is 56 patients in total, with 28 in each group.
segments.explanation: The calculation gives 56 per group. A consistent statement is: “The unrounded requirement of 55.68382 per group is rounded upward to 56, giving 112 analyzable patients in total.”

segments.text: To allow for 5% unavailable outcomes, 5% is added to 56 and the result is rounded down to 58 recruits per group, giving 116 recruits in total.
segments.explanation: The retained fraction is 0.95. The calculation should divide 56 by 0.95 and round upward: 59 recruits per group, or 118 in total. The report also needs a justification for the assumed 5% loss.
segments.heading: Recruitment and conclusion

segments.text: Screening records suggest 15 recruits per month after eligibility, availability and consent are considered. Recruitment is planned over eight months, with additional time for site opening. The trial will test whether the population pain-relief percentages differ between treatments.
segments.explanation: At 15 recruits per month, eight months provides capacity for 120 recruits, enough for the corrected total of 118. The stated conclusion matches the superiority test. The forecast should be supported by the screening records.

report.instructions: Four passages need correction. A reason and a proposed revision can be considered before selecting each passage to check the explanation.

segments.text: Standard care has an 80% discharge percentage
segments.explanation: This is the stated baseline for all three plans. Keeping it fixed makes the target differences comparable.

segments.text: A 20% relative increase in Plan A gives 100% discharged
segments.explanation: A relative increase of 20% gives 80% x 1.20 = 96%, an increase of 16 percentage points. Adding 20 percentage points would give 100%.

segments.text: Plan B's increase of 10 percentage points gives 90% discharged
segments.explanation: Adding 10 percentage points to 80% gives 90%. This is an absolute change.

segments.text: At the same 80% power, Plan B needs fewer patients than Plan A
segments.explanation: In these plans, detecting the smaller 10-point difference in Plan B requires more patients than detecting the 16-point difference in Plan A. The calculation also uses the two event percentages.

segments.text: Increasing power to 90% in Plan C reduces the required sample
segments.explanation: Plan C retains Plan A's event percentages and Type I error probability. Achieving the higher power requires more patients.

segments.text: For 56 analyzable patients per group and 5% expected missing outcomes, we plan to recruit 59 per group
segments.explanation: Dividing 56 by 0.95 and rounding upward gives 59 recruits per group.

segments.text: Anyone who switches treatment will automatically count as lost to follow-up
segments.explanation: A participant who switches treatment can still provide the four-week pain-relief outcome. For the effect of treatment assignment, that outcome remains in the participant's randomized group. Figure 3.1 shows treatment received and outcome availability separately.

segments.text: If expected losses are 10% in one group and 20% in the other, an overall 15% allowance will meet the expected analyzable requirement in both groups
segments.explanation: The groups need separate retention assumptions. For 56 analyzable patients, the recruitment calculations give 63 at 10% expected loss and 70 at 20%. With equal recruitment, the app uses 70 per group so that the higher-loss group meets the expected requirement.

segments.text: Recruiting extra participants will remove bias caused by missing outcomes
segments.explanation: Extra recruitment can protect the expected count. Missing-outcome bias depends on why outcomes are missing and how they are analyzed. Prevention, appropriate analysis and sensitivity analyses remain necessary.

segments.text: For a target mean difference of 2 fatigue score units and an SD of 4, Cohen's d is 0.50
segments.explanation: For this independent two-group comparison, d = 2 / 4 = 0.50.

segments.text: The corresponding two-group ANOVA therefore uses f = 0.50
segments.explanation: For the stated unadjusted comparison with two equally sized groups, f = d / 2 = 0.25. Entering f = 0.50 represents a mean difference of 4 units at SD 4.

segments.text: A software result labeled total sample size can be recorded as patients per group
segments.explanation: The output label determines what the count represents. For two equally sized groups, the total is twice the per-group count. The final report should state both counts explicitly.

segments.text: Selecting this unadjusted ANOVA automatically accounts for baseline fatigue scores
segments.explanation: Baseline-adjusted analysis requires a method and assumptions for the intended covariate adjustment. The simple two-group ANOVA calculation here contains no baseline covariate.

estimation_report.title: Activity: Review an estimation sample size calculation report

segments.text: The survey will estimate the percentage of outpatient clinic patients needing an interpreter, assessed at their next appointment.
segments.explanation: The population, quantity and assessment time are specified.

segments.text: With 80% power, 30% anticipated prevalence and a 6% margin of error, the sample size is 225.
segments.explanation: This estimates a population percentage with a chosen precision. Use 95% confidence and a margin of six percentage points. The normal approximation gives 1.96 squared times 0.30 times 0.70 divided by 0.06 squared, or 224.09, rounded upward to 225 completed assessments.

segments.text: The requirement is 225 patients per group.
segments.explanation: There is one population sample. The requirement is 225 completed assessments in total.

segments.text: The recruitment target is 225, allowing for 10% nonresponse.
segments.explanation: To obtain 225 completed assessments with 10% anticipated nonresponse, divide by 0.90. The target is 250 patients to approach.

segments.text: The calculation was performed with an online calculator.
segments.explanation: Identify the calculator and version or access date, procedure, inputs and interval method. Another reader should be able to reproduce the calculation and check its assumptions.
